THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company questioning the liability as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

2. Brief facts :
On 02.12.2013, at about 8.30 a.m., the deceased was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-52-H-2614 from Begur to Tavarekere towards Jogitopu,
when he reached near Jogitopu, met with an accident, due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-EH-2499 by its rider, due to which, the deceased fell down and sustained injuries all over the body and during the time of treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, the claimants being the dependants have filed the claim petition, seeking compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company and the learned counsel for the claimants.

4. The Tribunal after appreciation of oral and documentary evidence on record, has awarded a compensation of Rs.9,29,000/-, under various heads as follows:

Particulars

 1. Loss of dependency 8,64,000-00  2. Medical expenses 10,000-00  3. Transportation of dead body 10,000-00

5. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that the rider of the motor cycle did not produce the driving license as on the date and time of the accident.
Therefore, there is a violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance policy.
He has referred to Ex.P3-Charge Sheet for the offence of non-holding driving license as per Section 181 of the Motor Vehicle Act.
Therefore submitted that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Further submitted that the compensation granted is also on the higher side.
Therefore, prays to reduce the quantum of compensation.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondents-claimants and the learned counsel for the owner of the offending vehicle have justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
7. In the present case, the deceased died due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle.

Ex.P3 is the charge sheet, in which the Investigating Officer had found after investigation that the rider of the motor cycle was not holding driving license to ride the motor cycle and accordingly, offence falls under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

But, the Tribunal in findings at Paragraph-19 of the judgment and Award, has wrongly observed that the charge sheet does not disclose the offence of non producing of driving license by the rider of the offending vehicle.
This observation of the Tribunal at paragraph-19 is perverse, as contrary to the evidence on record.
Ex.P3- charge sheet reveals that the offence against the rider of the motor cycle is that he was not holding driving license.
Therefore, in order to controvert this, the owner neither produced the driving licence before the police in reply to the notice issued under Section 134 of M.V. Act nor produced before the Tribunal.

Therefore, the Insurance Company has discharged its burden proving the rider was not holding driving license as on the date and time of the accident, but at the same time, the owner of the offending vehicle even though appeared and contested the claim petition, did not produce the driving license before the Tribunal.

However, as per Sub-Section (2) of Section 149 of the MV Act,
the Insurance Company is able to take defense and established successfully, but as per Sub- Sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of MV Act and also as per the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh reported in 2004 ACJ 1, Pappu and others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in (2018)3 SCC 208 and decision of the Full Bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and another reported in ILR 2020 KAR 2239, the principle of pay and recovery is applied since the claimants are third parties.

8. The deceased was a bachelor.

The Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd of the income towards living and The Manager vs Shri Shafiulla Baig on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60685749/
4 personal expenditure.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that 50%
ought to have been deducted since the deceased was bachelor.

Taking into consideration the submission of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the accident was occurred in the year 2014, the notional income ought to have been taken as Rs.8,500/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken Rs.6,000/- per month only.
Further, the Tribunal has not added income towards loss of future prospects in life.
Further more, the compensation awarded are less.

Therefore, even though the claimants have not preferred appeal and if the compensation is to be re-assessed upon the parameters upon the facts of the case, then over all compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and proper which needs no interference.
The claimants have not filed appeal for enhancement, at the same time, the Tribunal committed an error in not adding the income towards loss of future prospects in life.
Therefore, considering the over all facts and circumstances and amount of compensation arrived at by the Tribunal is found to be just and proper.
Therefore, on quantum, the appeal is dismissed.

9. The Tribunal has granted interest at the rate of 9% per annum and the same is scaled down to 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

10. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 27.01.2016 passed in MVC No.667/2014 by the Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Tumakuru, is hereby modified only to the extent of liability is concerned.
